entries.summary: The Santo Niño Basilica is a Catholic minor basilica in Cebu City, founded by Augustinian friars in 1565. Its continuing religious role and association with the Santo Niño image make it a central downtown heritage destination.
overview: The Basilica Minore del Santo Niño de Cebu was founded in 1565 by Augustinian friars Andrés de Urdaneta and Diego de Herrera. Its history is closely associated with devotion to the Santo Niño de Cebu. The basilica remains a religious place, so a visitor interested in its architecture should also consider worship taking place. The nearby Magellan’s Cross landmark is a separate stop.
highlights: Learn the basilica’s association with Santo Niño devotion.

entries.summary: The National Museum of the Philippines–Cebu occupies the 1910 Aduana building in the city’s port and heritage district. Its former customs-house architecture is part of the visit, alongside the museum’s permanent and changing galleries.
overview: The National Museum of the Philippines–Cebu opened to the public in August 2023. Its building began as Cebu’s Customs House, or Aduana, designed by William Edward Parsons and constructed in 1910. The property later became Malacañan sa Sugbo before conversion into a museum. This layered history makes the building itself an important part of the visit. The museum describes permanent galleries on the first floor and changing galleries on the second. Its address is A. Pigafetta Street in Barangay San Roque, within the port and heritage district. Check the institution’s current information when planning around a particular temporary exhibition.
highlights: Look at the reused Aduana building.
Explore the museum’s permanent and changing gallery spaces.

entries.summary: The Heritage of Cebu Monument is a sculptural tableau in Parian, Cebu City. It represents people, buildings and events from Cebu’s history, bringing several historical subjects together in one outdoor monument.
overview: Also called the Parian Monument, the Heritage of Cebu Monument was built between 1997 and 2000. Its sculptural composition depicts figures, buildings and events associated with Cebu, spanning subjects from the Battle of Mactan to Pedro Calungsod’s beatification. A visit is an opportunity to look closely at the tableau’s individual scenes rather than treating it as a single statue.
highlights: Look for individual historical scenes in the sculptural tableau.

entries.summary: Kawasan Falls is a multi-stage waterfall on the Kawasan River in Badian, southern Cebu. Mountain-spring water flows through a gorge and a series of cascades, creating a river setting distinct from Cebu’s beaches.
overview: Kawasan Falls forms part of the Kawasan River in Badian. Water from Kabukalan Spring passes through the Kawasan gorge and onward toward the Matutinao River and Tañon Strait. Outdoor and water activities depend on current local conditions and operating arrangements; a visitor video is a record of one visit, not a determination of conditions on your travel day.
